steps.title: Start with everyday life.
steps.description: A family wants to help their child express a choice during a familiar routine. They describe what the child already does, what interests them and where support helps.
steps.meaning: Everyday observations give the care team context.

steps.title: Bring the observations together.
steps.description: The family and professionals review the starting point and agree a useful goal. Pinnacle describes the Personal Development Kernel as the child-specific record connecting measurements, context and responses.
steps.meaning: The care team checks the goal and the support appropriate to this child.

steps.title: Make the starting point understandable.
steps.description: The overall AbilityScore® report and seven readiness views help organise the discussion. The important connection is from the report to an agreed everyday goal.
steps.meaning: Explore what each report is for below. No individual child’s results are displayed here.

steps.title: Turn the goal into guided practice.
steps.description: The documented Everyday Therapy™ programme links selected techniques with goals. In this illustration, the care team explains a communication activity within a familiar routine and agrees how the family can take part.
steps.meaning: The activity, support and practice schedule are agreed with the care team.

steps.title: What happened during practice?
steps.description: Feedback connects the experience at home with the next review. Try either response to see how the discussion can change.
steps.meaning: This demonstration does not assess a child, prescribe an activity or generate a treatment plan.

steps.title: Use the experience to shape the next plan.
steps.description: The care team reviews feedback, adjusts goals or support, and discusses the next assessment. Monthly reassessment is described in the reviewed methodology and walkthrough.
steps.meaning: Look for meaningful changes in communication, routines, learning and participation, alongside the scores.

reports.name: AbilityScore® / TherapeuticAI® report
reports.question: Which abilities should we prioritise, and why?

reports.name: Speech Readiness Index
reports.meaning: A focused view to discuss communication priorities.
reports.question: How can we support communication in everyday routines?

reports.name: Behavior Readiness Index
reports.meaning: A focused view to discuss behaviour and participation.
reports.question: What helps my child feel comfortable and take part?

reports.name: Motor Readiness Index
reports.meaning: A focused view to discuss movement-related abilities.
reports.question: Which movement skills matter for my child’s routines?

reports.name: Study/IQ Readiness Index
reports.meaning: The report’s named view of readiness for learning.
reports.question: What support could make learning more accessible?

reports.name: School Readiness Index
reports.meaning: A focused view to discuss preparation and support for school.
reports.question: What would help my child participate at school?

reports.name: Self-Sufficiency Index
reports.meaning: A focused view to discuss growing everyday independence.
reports.question: Which everyday task could my child do with less help?

reports.name: Mainstream Readiness Index
reports.meaning: A focused view to discuss participation with other people.
reports.question: What support would help my child join in with others?
